# SOCIAL.md — Launch Day Posts & Replies

## LinkedIn Post (158 words)

Threadmark is available today on Windows and macOS.

I built it because I kept losing track of which PDF supported which claim in my own research. The core idea is simple: you point the app at a folder of PDFs and notes, it builds a searchable map, and every sentence in its summaries links back to the exact passage it came from. Click a sentence, the source opens at the right page. No upload, no cloud processing — everything runs locally.

$12/month after a 14-day trial. Linux is under investigation but not promised.

If you work with dense PDFs and need to trace claims to evidence, it might save you time. If not, that's fine too.

---

## Bluesky Post (274 characters)

Threadmark launches today: a desktop app that turns folders of research PDFs into a local, searchable evidence map. Every summary sentence links to its source passage. $12/mo after 14-day trial. Win/macOS now; Linux being investigated. threadmark.app

---

## Instagram Caption (102 words)

Threadmark is live. Point it at a folder of research PDFs and notes, get a searchable map where every summary sentence links to its exact source passage. Click a claim, see the evidence. All local, nothing leaves your machine. $12/month after 14-day trial. Windows and macOS ready; Linux TBD.

Built this because I got tired of Ctrl-F'ing through 40 PDFs to find one quote. If you do literature reviews, policy work, or any research where traceability matters, maybe it helps.

#Threadmark #ResearchTools #LocalFirst #EvidenceMapping

---

## Comment Replies

### LinkedIn: "Is this just another chatbot wrapping my documents?"

No — there's no chatbot. Threadmark extracts and summarizes, then links each sentence to the passage it came from. You read the summary; if you want the context, click and the PDF opens at that page. No generation, just retrieval and compression.

### LinkedIn: "Can a university buy seats for a lab?"

Not yet — current licensing is per-user via the website. Volume or institutional options aren't built out. Happy to discuss requirements if you email support@threadmark.app.

### Bluesky: "no linux, no deal"

Understood. Linux is being investigated but I'm not promising a timeline. If you're on Linux and want to be notified when there's something concrete, there's a "notify me" field on the site.

### Bluesky: "Does local mean you train on my papers anyway?"

No training, no upload, no telemetry on document content. The app indexes and summarizes entirely on your machine. The only network call is the license check at startup.

### Instagram: "I paid and the app has been stuck indexing for two hours."

That shouldn't happen — sorry. First, try restarting the app; indexing resumes where it left off. If it's still stuck, email support@threadmark.app with your OS and rough folder size and I'll help diagnose. No account details needed.

### Instagram: "Would this work for a literature review in Japanese?"

Yes, if the PDFs contain selectable text (not scanned images). The summarization handles Japanese, and source linking works the same way. OCR for scanned pages isn't built in yet.
